findings.title: Critical closed Tate radius invalidates exponential and unit assertions in Lemma 5.7

source_locations.claim: alpha=1/(p-1) for odd p; scalar exponential on p^alpha m_K
logarithmic coordinate isomorphism, exponential inverse and log(1+T)/T unit

counterexample.parameters: p=3, K=C_3, X=(P^1_K)^an, canonical lift from Q_3, any allowed Exp, E=O_X with theta=0, V=O_X, toric unit annulus U, R=K<x,x^-1>, B=O_U, J=(partial), pi^2=3.
assumptions_verified: Coherent torsion-free B and zero-section condition on J
counterexample.calculation: For n=3^k, v_3(pi^n/n!)=1/2; coefficients fail to tend to zero. With t0=zeta_3-1, t0^2+3t0+3=0, v_3(t0)=1/2, log(1+t0)=0, and log(1+t0)/t0=0.
counterexample.scope: Counterexample to auxiliary algebra assertions, not to final comparison theorem.

findings.general_proof: For odd p, n=p^k gives v_p(n!)=(p^k-1)/(p-1), so v_p(pi^n/n!)=1/(p-1). A primitive pth-root-minus-one has that boundary valuation and annihilates log(1+T)/T.
counterevidence_considered: The paper's earlier exponential domain is open, correctly
Smallness after applying a module action does not shrink the universal Tate algebra
Further etale localization can support a changed radius but does not change the current radius
Capital Exp is not an analytic inverse on the closed boundary
The p=2 choice alpha=2 is strictly safe
No variables in dimension zero means this obstruction does not apply
findings.dependency: Invalid step completes Lemma 5.7, used to prove Theorem 5.5 and intro Theorem 1.4.
findings.impact: Core cohomological proof gap for odd p; categorical equivalence and comparison statements not disproved.

repair.precise_statement: For rational beta>1/(p-1), exp-1 and log(1+T) are inverse analytic coordinates on the closed radius p^{-beta} disc; log(1+T)/T is a unit and coordinatewise Koszul rescaling is invertible.
repair.boundary: Application to global proof requires explicit stronger local factorization/smallness and compatible lifted modules; complete global incorporation not independently verified.

unresolved_claims: Full global incorporation of strict-radius repair
acceptance_corrections: Separated acceptance of the demonstrated closed-radius defect from certification of a complete globally repaired proof of Theorem5.5. Major and local repair scope unchanged.

independent_acceptance_check.scope: Focused acceptance of existing F01 in the exact 52-page publisher PDF, with bounded static corroboration from the pinned author source. No author-code execution, whole-paper rereview or assertion of complete author/publisher-text equivalence.

checks.item: Critical closed radius and admissible hypotheses
checks.result: For odd p, the exponential's rescaled coefficients along n=p^k fail to tend to zero in the asserted Tate algebra. The boundary root of log(1+T)/T independently prevents the claimed unit property. The zero-Higgs example with p=3 and the stated smooth proper setting satisfies the relevant assumptions; the objection does not rely on a discarded coherent quotient.

The valuation derivation and existing exact-arithmetic valuation output were checked; the finite computation is treated only as a consistency check, not as the proof of nonconvergence. Lemma 5.7 is directly used in the core cohomological comparison, Theorem 5.5/1.4.

On a strictly smaller closed disc with beta>1/(p-1), the exponential/logarithm coordinates and logarithmic unit have the proved convergence and invertibility properties. Incorporation into the full global construction remains explicitly unverified. One Major proof defect stands; neither a false comparison theorem nor a false categorical correspondence is inferred.

The report now requires the remaining global checks before claiming a complete repaired proof of Theorem 5.5, rather than before accepting the already demonstrated local defect. Current focused acceptance and pending human adjudication are stated consistently.

independent_acceptance_check.result: Accepted after correction of the repair-scope/acceptance wording. F01 remains Major with a verified local analytic repair and an explicit global proof boundary.
